question: A body of mass m and a body of mass 4m are dropped from the same height, the ratio of the time taken by the two bodies to reach the ground would be: (Air resistance is neglected)
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 : 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the absence of air resistance, the acceleration due to gravity (g) is constant for all objects regardless of their masses.
 
• The time taken to fall from a certain height depends only on the height and the gravitational acceleration, not on the mass of the object.
 
• Both bodies, one of mass m and the other of mass 4m, will experience the same gravitational pull and will fall at the same rate.

• **Gravitational Acceleration (g)**

 
 
• The acceleration of an object due to the Earth's gravity is approximately 9.8 m/s².
 
• It is denoted by the symbol "g" and is a constant value near the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion**
 
 
• The equations of motion describe the relationship between the displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time of an object in motion.

• **Mass Independence**
 
 
• In the absence of air resistance, the mass of an object does not affect the time it takes to fall to the ground.
 
• This principle was famously demonstrated by Galileo's experiments in the late 16th century.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall**
 
 
• Free fall is the motion of an object where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In free fall, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass.
